newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S., security pacts seen as key to Asian peace.
newsitem.headline: U.S., security pacts seen as key to Asian peace.

text.p: A continued United States military presence and key regional security pacts were vital to boosting stability in the Asia-Pacific, British Defence Minister Michael Portillo said on Monday.

"The U.S. presence and engagement...are fundamental to the region's security," Portillo said in a speech to the Australian Defence Force Academy. "We strongly welcome their (U.S.) continued determination to play this key role."
Portillo also said a recent security pact between Australia and neighbouring Indonesia was essential to increasing regional security.
Portillo reaffirmed Britain's commitment to the Five Power Defence Arrangement linking Australia, Britain, Malaysia, New Zealand and Singapore, which he said was an important security measure.
Portillo, in Australia for meetings with his ministerial counterpart and defence industry officials, urged greater defence transparency and co-operation between countries in the region.
"Increased transparency in defence matters can help to break down suspicions that countries have about their neighbours' intentions," Portillo said.
"Some have expressed concern over a new arms race starting in this region," he said.
Portillo said releasing white papers setting out defence policy and planning would help ease regional concerns.
